We were pleased to welcome Ray Tooby, on leave from the Army, also Denis Brickwood, the well-known Mitcham A.C. runner, who has now joined us first-claim.
Denis Brickwood, who is now first-claim to us having resigned from Mitcham A.C., also ran quite well and will be a most useful addition to our team strength when he is qualified.

Denis Brickwood and Bill Lucas ran steadily throughout the race to finish third and fourth, and were well backed up by the Bishop brothers, who are most certainly our keenest supporters at all our fixtures.

The course was about 8 miles and the first man home was Archie Bedford, who beat a couple of Walton boys, with Len Adams and Denis Brickwood next home for us.

Len Adams was another to run well and he deservedly won the first handicap award. Denis Brickwood also gained his first club prize by finishing second in the handicap and Steve Charlton gained third place.

Outstanding among the performances of our runners was Denis Brickwood's fine effort in finishing 3rd in a fast time. Mac was not entirely fit on the day, but finished quite well up, Arthur Whitehead completing our team, which gained third position.
The meeting was opened by Denis Brickwood outlining the somewhat docile outlook of the runners to-day which had its reflection in a degree of Club stagnation.
For about 13 miles he ran with Denis Brickwood, and this pair, despite numerous challenges, maintained a perfect pace and ran steadily through the field.

Mike Stearman ran well seeing that, under the new E.C.C.U. rules, he is still a junior and he pays tribute to the way he was helped along by Denis Brickwood, who seems to be regaining some of his old form.
Then followed Bob Taylor, Denis Brickwood and J.
Eric Herbert 15th, and Denis Brickwood 16th, and our sixth man was J. Masters 21st, and as this was the latter's first County race, he did very well and should improve with further experience.

Over a very heavy course of about 8 miles, Ray Tooby was first home in 49 mins. 44 secs., with Dunckley, of the Poly., second, and Bob Taylor third. Denis Brickwood and Eddie Short also ran well, but the rest of our lads found the heavy going not to their liking.

This brings up the point about all those entered who can turn out should come along with their togs in case they are required, and in any event, they can do a good job of work round the course in their track suits, as did Denis Brickwood at this race.

Then came Denis Brickwood 30th, and as Denis was placed 22nd in the 1939 race, we think it a remarkable achievement for him to drop only eight places after a lapse of 14 years, and just shows what can be done with properly applied training methods.
Denis Brickwood ran well to finish 55th, with Eddie Short 75th, and Eddie only ran in order that we should field a full team of nine men, as he has been troubled with an ankle injury.
Denis Brickwood dropped a place on the 8th stage to Baverstock of the Beagles, and Len Herbert could only keep this position on the 9th leg.

At 4½ miles Denis Brickwood was nicely placed 29th and running strongly but steadily. Arthur Whitehead, Jock McDonald and Bill Wortley were close behind, while the rest of our lads were among the 100s.

Olding 37.06 and Ron Linstead, yet a junior, 37.25, but as Olding is only second claim and therefore not eligible for a Club Championship, Ron Linstead took the 2nd medal and Dennis Brickwood (37.33) 3rd.

Our first man home was Jim Masters 21st, followed by Stan Gawler 29th D. Brickwood 36th, C.

Bedford,our junior D.Baulch,L.Herbert Bill Lucas, Dennis Brickwood, Len Bishop, Eddie Short, S. Gawler and Mike Stearman all of whom were to give the selectors some head aches when trying to find the best team for the approaching National Brighton Relay.

Our Cross Country Captain Dennis Brickwood, who in 1937 had started Mitcham A.C. on a winning sequence in this event by an inches decision over our own Arthur Allum, was performing for the first time in this race in Belgrave colours and although chased by two very promising runners in the shape of D…

Not far behind Chas. was "[illegible]umbo" Masters in 41st place, a good performance especially in view of his recent foot injury. Dennis Brickwood running in his usual steady manner, was our next man to finish coming 73rd.

Len Adams however, running his first 20, was still moving very well and Ken Stimpson, running his first long distance race, was surprising everyone by his excellent showing and was still more than a minute ahead of Dennis Brickwood at 15.

Denis Brickwood running in his usual manner, took Eric Gebbett, who was making his first appearance in long distance running, with him for the first twelve miles when Eric began to tire and Denis ran on to be fairly well placed and followed by Eric who had recovered to finish within standard time.

Denis Brickwood, who came into the team at the last minute due to Chris Roffey being unfit, again took the Redhill stage but unfortunately had to contend with Withers of Blackheath, a very promising performer who produced the fastest time of the day on this leg and in so doing took his team into 3rd place.
Denis Brickwood wrecked himself on some barbed wire and Arthur Penstone cut his leg badly. How he managed to carry on running for three miles is beyond understanding.

The position of the leaders was maintained down Copse Hill but it was noticeable that Archie Bedford, Charlie Smart and Denis Brickwood, who had all made a steady start, were making progress through the field.
Rolls, D. Brickwood and Charlie Smart had a very easy win, with the last named showing great form in returning a lap time of 19.46.

Past winners were in attendance, including our own Denis Brickwood, Bill Lucas, Charlie Walker and Roger Alsop. Fine words were spoken and toasts drunk — it was good old traditional harrier evening.

…lcomes were also extended to Pam Davies and Dave McMillan back from severe illness and horrific injury respectively; to Dennis Brickwood our cross country captain in the 50's and still looking capable of showing many in the Club a clean pair of heels; and to special guest and friend from Herne Hill…
This was followed by 3rd in the Southern and 6th in the National with the lead man on each occasion being Jack Brown with Charlie Walker, Len and Alan Bishop, along with Dennis Brickwood in the team.
